business_problem: Fujitsu needed a highly accurate Japanese large language model for customers in regulated industries that handle confidential data and strict compliance requirements, but building that model required advanced infrastructure, large language datasets, and specialized AI expertise it wanted to accelerate through a trusted partner.
solution_summary: Fujitsu partnered with Cohere to build Takane, a privately deployed Japanese large language model based on the Cohere Command series. Cohere provided training support and technical expertise so Fujitsu could create a model tuned for Japanese enterprise language and capable of world-class performance on the JGLUE benchmark. Takane is designed for high-stakes legal, finance, healthcare, government, and manufacturing workflows where accuracy and security matter, and it processes long text with enough precision to streamline document-heavy operations. The model can extract key details and transform unstructured information into JSON, HTML, Markdown, and CSV, while also supporting multilingual work in languages such as German, Chinese, and Portuguese. Fujitsu now delivers Takane through Fujitsu Kozuchi and its Data Intelligence PaaS so regulated customers can adopt secure generative AI inside broader digital-transformation programs.

data_flow: Regulated-industry text and business documents enter Takane, the model applies Japanese-centric language understanding and reasoning to process or extract the content, outputs structured formats such as JSON or CSV when needed, and Fujitsu exposes those capabilities through Kozuchi and DI PaaS for downstream enterprise workflows.
business_outcome: Takane is now part of Fujitsu's digital transformation offerings and gives Japanese businesses in regulated industries a secure way to automate document-heavy workflows, improve decision-making, and deliver better customer experiences while Fujitsu accelerates development of high-impact AI applications.
